This aligns my highest-preference school with my highest-priority school, giving me the best strategic position, and follows correctly with my secondary priorities at x and z.

Under DA, truthfully ranking schools according to one's actual preferences is a dominant strategy — misrepresenting preferences cannot lead to a better outcome than truth-telling, regardless of one's priority levels or other applicants' preferences.

Looking at my priorities: I have priority 4 (lowest) at w and x, and priority 3 at y and z. Since most other applicants also prefer y > x > w > z, competition for y and x will be intense, and my mediocre priority there means I might not get my top choices.
